question: with the hub cutoff bounding auto_link_by_entity (was 89.5% of writer wall, O(N^2) per build), does the >150k-gene rate decay persist, and what drives the residual?
method: rate-vs-N from genes.observed_at (stamped worker-side at tag time — measures tagging throughput)
writer instantaneous rate from the 1,352 cumulative progress lines in rebuild_cutoff200_v2.err.log (measures the single-writer drain — the decaying component)

findings.o_n2_refuted: the rate ~ C/N signature of the uncapped build (61 → 4.9 g/s) is GONE at cutoff=200; worker tagging throughput is flat ~50 g/s from N=20k to 580k; the writer declines mildly and ~linearly in N

writer_rate_curve_inst_g_per_s.note: N = genes processed (incl. dedup overwrites); local wall times; v2c sequential bed build shared the machine until 09:27; tagging workers drained ~09:40 — the 29→38 jump at 09:40 is worker-CPU contention ending, not N-dependence

findings.clean_tail: writer alone, 479k→656k processed: 38.4 → 32.7 g/s = 26.0 → 30.6 ms/gene; +4.6 ms per 177k genes — linear per-insert cost growth
findings.residual_root_cause: per-upsert `DELETE FROM filename_index WHERE gene_id = ?` (storage/indexes.py sync_filename_index) is a full-table SCAN — the table has only the (filename_stem, gene_id) PK and idx_filename_stem, no gene_id index — so the delete is O(N) rows per insert

evidence.explain_plan: SCAN filename_index (571,999 rows on the finished bed)
reconciliation: old uncapped build, py-spy at 289k genes: filename DELETE = 6.6% of writer wall; terminal 204 ms/gene × 6.6% ≈ 13.5 ms ≈ a warm scan of the then-~280k-row table
clean-tail slope +4.6 ms per 177k genes ≈ the incremental scan cost of 177k added rows
at 572k rows the scan is essentially the whole non-base writer budget (30.6 ms/gene total)

findings.fix: idx_filename_gene ON filename_index(gene_id) — commit a39532f on this branch (filename_anchor.ensure_schema); content-neutral; existing beds pick it up on next open
findings.projection: with the index, the writer's N-dependent term drops to O(log N); bulk builds become tagging-bound at the flat ~50 g/s worker ceiling (~3.3 h for this 517k-file bed vs 5.0 h measured)
